editorial:
Ever have one of those mornings where everything goes wrong? Rachel is a divorced mom already running late when she honks at a stranger in traffic. That one small moment turns into a nightmare when the man behind the wheel decides she needs to be taught a lesson. What follows is a tense, fast-moving thriller that turns an ordinary commute into a fight for survival. Russell Crowe plays the mysterious driver with a scary calm that makes every scene feel dangerous, and Caren Pistorius keeps you rooting for Rachel as the danger keeps growing. The movie wastes no time getting to the point, and the stakes feel real because the threat could happen to anyone on the road.

The action is brutal and the pacing rarely slows down, which keeps you on edge the whole time. Some moments feel a bit over the top, and the story does not dig very deep into why the villain is so angry. Still, if you enjoy intense thrillers that keep your heart racing, this one delivers.
endingExplained: In the final act, Rachel learns the driver has been killing people connected to her, including her lawyer and brother, as part of his revenge plan. He traps her and her son at home, but Rachel fights back. With Kyle's help, she stabs the killer to death, ending his rampage. The movie closes with Rachel and her son safe, having survived the terrifying ordeal together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves road rage thrillers and edge-of-your-seat suspense.
